subject: Day 33: head control improving; visual tracking widens
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 33. Head lifts during tummy time can now reach 10-20 seconds at a stretch. Tracking is widening; many infants follow objects across most of the visual field by week five.

Action items
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is on the calendar (target day 56-70). AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Verify Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit is scheduled — about nine days from today. ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- If returning to work in 7-11 weeks, lock the daycare or nanny start date. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Refill infant acetaminophen if low; the 2-month vaccine visit is approaching. AAP HealthyChildren on fever: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Sustained head lifts; wider visual tracking; social smiles; cluster fussiness in the evenings.
- [low concern] Hiccups; wet sneezing; a quiet startle.
- [monitor] A head tilt that always turns the same way, or a flat spot developing — reposition and raise it at the next visit if it persists.
- [call within 24h] Sustained feeding refusal; bloody-mucus stool; fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Pass a high-contrast object slowly through a full 180-degree arc 8-12 inches from his face to encourage wide visual tracking. AAP HealthyChildren on movement, birth to three months: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Sing the same short song at the same daily moment — bath, first wake — so predictable live music supports pattern recognition. Gerry, Unrau, Trainor, Dev Sci 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day; vary floor, chest-incline, and forearm football-hold positions. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Take a carrier walk outside; keep his face visible and his airway clear with his chin off his chest.

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: peak crying.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
